subject.title: [Feature]: Add a secure way to pair dynamically autoscaled worked nodes in K8s

question: Should OpenClaw accept a Kubernetes ServiceAccount/TokenReview worker-auth mode that can bypass interactive node pairing, and what fail-closed allowlist, audience, issuer, TLS/CA, and revocation policy must it enforce?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but implementing it changes gateway auth, protocol, config, deployment docs, and the node-pairing trust boundary; automation cannot choose that security policy safely.

options.title: Approve a narrow SA Trust design
options.body: Define a fail-closed Kubernetes worker identity contract and then accept a focused implementation with config, protocol, docs, and tests.

options.title: Fold into distributed runtime auth
options.body: Keep this issue open but make the broader distributed-runtime milestone own the worker-auth contract before implementation.

options.title: Decline core K8s auth mode
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide Kubernetes-specific worker trust should stay outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SA Trust design
recommendation.body: Define a fail-closed Kubernetes worker identity contract and then accept a focused implementation with config, protocol, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent review context on this exact issue and recent gateway/auth documentation history, making them the best available routing owner for the security-boundary decision.
